hook.text: If 'John killed the spider,' then 'the spider is dead' must be true. No way around it.

buildup.text: Entailment is a meaning relation: sentence A entails sentence B if B must be true whenever A is.

discovery.text: Entailments are built into word meanings—'kill' entails 'die,' 'buy' entails 'pay.'

twist.text: Entailment is one-directional: the spider being dead doesn't entail that John killed it.

climax.text: Lawyers and logicians use entailment to test whether conclusions follow from premises.

punchline.text: Some truths ride on the back of others.

quiz.question: What does entailment mean?
options: If A is true, B must be true
